title: Sea Surface Temperature of the mid-Piacenzian Ocean: A Data-Model Comparison
problem: Climate model simulations of the warm mid-Piacenzian period show significant discord with palaeoenvironmental reconstructions, particularly by failing to reproduce the large magnitude of high-latitude warming documented in the geological record.
method: The paper proposes a systematic data-model comparison, contrasting sea surface temperature anomalies from an ensemble of eight climate model simulations against a palaeoenvironmental reconstruction to identify regional discordances and evaluate model performance for the mid-Piacenzian warm period.
task: The task is to systematically compare mid-Piacenzian sea surface temperatures from an ensemble of climate model simulations with palaeoenvironmental data reconstructions to identify key areas of agreement and discord between the two datasets.
innovation: This paper presents the first systematic comparison of mid-Piacenzian sea surface temperatures between an ensemble of eight climate models (PlioMIP) and a palaeoenvironmental reconstruction (PRISM), identifying key regional disagreements that have led to improved strategies for both experimental design and palaeoenvironmental data refinement.

kg_extraction_triplets.paragraph: This area is, of course, complex given that a myriad of strong feedbacks can affect the region, including changes in sea ice, the Gulf Stream current, Atlantic meridional overturning, and even the storm tracks.

This area is, of course, complex given that a myriad of strong feedbacks can affect the region, including changes in sea ice, the Gulf Stream current, Atlantic meridional overturning, and even the storm tracks.

A second region of offset between the Aммм and APRISM exists in the mid- to high northern latitudes. The majority of sites in Figure 3 (area c) are from the North Atlantic. The extensive warming at high latitudes in the North Atlantic has been repeatedly documen- ted9,27,28,45 and is also seen in terrestrial archives of surface air tem- perature (e.g. 56,57). Mid-latitude sites (410, 548, 552, 606, 607, 608 and 610) are the very highest confidence sites in the PRISM3 data set, and the large inter-model spread in this region may be due to the highly variable position of the Gulf Stream—North Atlantic Drift and the resolution of the different models⁴⁵.

Four sites in Figure 3 (area c) are outside the North Atlantic. Sites 579 and 580 are located in the North Pacific Kuroshio Extension. Analysis of the diatom assemblages at both sites suggests moderate warming over present day conditions within the PRISM interval8,13. Some but not all PlioMIP simulations pick up this North Pacific warming (relative to PI conditions) (Figure 1). New faunal data from ODP Site 1208, located beneath the Kuroshio Extension, show little change in mean annual temperature relative to present day but suggest greatly reduced seasonality (5°C), with winter temperatures warmer during the Pliocene (Supplementary material).

Sites 1236 and 1237 are both situated on the Nazca Ridge. Site 1236 is located just seaward of the main path of the cool, northward flowing Peru-Chile Current while Site 1237 is located near the eastern edge of the current and associated upwelling. Proxy SST data show warmer upwelling conditions during the Pliocene than exist today in the region, analogous to the upwelling region off the Pacific coast of North America (Figure 2).
